::: {.callout-tip}
## Why This Matters
Northwest China's first 8-inch specialty-process semiconductor line — another facility this tracker missed in its first passes, illustrating that under-construction projects outside the handful of best-covered hubs (Shanghai, Beijing, Shenzhen) are easy to miss without deliberately searching provincial and industry-trade coverage rather than only the most prominent national outlets.
:::

**Chinese name:** 陕西电子芯业时代科技有限公司 (Shǎnxī Diànzǐ Xīnyè Shídài Kējì Yǒuxiàn Gōngsī)

## What does this facility make?

Industrial-grade and automotive-grade power semiconductors — IGBTs and silicon carbide (SiC) chips — for EVs, renewable energy storage, and AI data center power systems, not logic or memory.

## Why does it matter?

A reminder that China's fab build-out is not only about advanced logic and memory — mature-node power semiconductors for the EV and renewable-energy supply chains are a large, separate wave of construction with their own set of projects, mostly outside the export-control narrative entirely.

## Project Timeline

- **Dec 2025** — Phase 1 (¥3.2 billion, 50,000 wafers/month design capacity) completes and enters production
- **Sep 2026** — Phase 2 construction preparation begins, formal start targeted for Q3 2026, under a stated ¥19 billion total investment plan through 2030
